<execute-bead>
  <instructions>
You are executing one bead inside an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the completion contract — every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file you can point to after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

The bead is too big when any of these holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs as separate top-level deliverables.
- Description names multiple feature-sized sub-pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across more than ~5 files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, treat Step 0 as a split-first pass and favor child-bead scoping before implementation.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, decomposed children may split once more, and third-level splits must be rejected with an explanation.

If too big, decompose — do not attempt the work:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child slice (focused title, description, AC; copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'` so the decomposition is visible.
4. Write `.ddx/executions/20260507T023755-5dbafdce/no_changes_rationale.txt` listing each child ID and slice, then stop.

A clean decomposition is a successful attempt. Do not mix partial implementation with decomposition.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC against concrete evidence (test name, file path, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- If you cannot finish, write `.ddx/executions/20260507T023755-5dbafdce/no_changes_rationale.txt` (what is done, what blocks, what a follow-up needs) before exiting. No commit and no rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`. A well-justified no_changes beats a bad commit.

## no_changes contract

If you write `.ddx/executions/20260507T023755-5dbafdce/no_changes_rationale.txt`, it MUST carry one of:

- `verification_command: <one-line shell command>` — the loop runs it (cwd = project root, 60s); exit 0 closes the bead, non-zero rejects.
- `status: needs_investigation` + `reason: <why>` — bead stays open for triage.

Bare rationales ("nothing to do") are rejected.

## Reports

Freestanding artifacts (investigation reports, findings docs) go under `.ddx/executions/20260507T023755-5dbafdce/` (the per-attempt evidence directory under `.ddx/executions/`). **Never write reports to `/tmp` or any path outside the repository** — out-of-repo paths are invisible to the post-merge reviewer and cause BLOCK on missing evidence. If the bead names a specific in-repo path, use it; else default to `.ddx/executions/20260507T023755-5dbafdce/<short-name>.md`. Stage and commit the report alongside code.

## Bead overrides project defaults

The bead description and AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and conservative project defaults (YAGNI, DOWITYTD, no-docs-unless-asked) in this worktree — write whatever the bead asks for.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized; running it corrupts the bead queue.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other project-instructions files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator — do not keep exploring or testing.
  </instructions>
  <bead id="fizeau-b73fed1a">
    <title>Bias correlation IDs to sticky server instances</title>
    <description>
Use validated CorrelationID as the sticky route key and bind it to a server instance, not to model identity. Sticky affinity is a score bonus after eligibility, not a hard pin. Related requests should prefer the same server across model changes when that server remains eligible.
    </description>
    <acceptance>
1. The sticky lease map keys validated CorrelationID to server_instance with TTL/expiry behavior.
2. Repeated ResolveRoute/Execute requests with the same CorrelationID prefer the same server instance across different eligible models.
3. Stickiness never makes an ineligible candidate eligible and can be outweighed by hard saturation or severe performance/utilization pressure.
4. RouteDecision/RouteStatus expose sticky status, server_instance, reason, and bonus without leaking raw sensitive keys in operator JSON.
5. go test ./internal/routing ./internal/serviceimpl ./cmd/fiz -run "Sticky|Correlation|ServerInstance|Lease" passes.
    </acceptance>
    <notes>
Cleared stale execute-loop failure from the pre-v0.10.11 config parser error: grendel-rapid-mlx used type rapid-mlx before Fizeau accepted that provider type. Historical execution events are retained; queue eligibility should now be governed by status and dependencies.
    </notes>
    <labels>area:routing, area:service, kind:task</labels>

Implemented and committed as `0ab6b6c5` (`fix: bias sticky routes to server instances [fizeau-b73fed1a]`).

What changed:
- Sticky leases now key off the validated correlation ID only, with TTL/expiry behavior in [`internal/routehealth/lease_store.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/internal/routehealth/lease_store.go).
- Routing now applies a sticky-affinity score bonus after eligibility instead of hard-reusing a previous selection, in [`internal/routing/engine.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/internal/routing/engine.go) and [`internal/routing/score.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/internal/routing/score.go).
- `RouteStickyState` now exposes `bonus` alongside status, server instance, and reason without exposing the raw key, in [`service.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/service.go), [`service_events.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/service_events.go), and [`internal/session/event.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/internal/session/event.go).
- The service now threads correlation IDs into routing, records sticky leases by server instance, and keeps session/event projections aligned in [`service_routing.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/service_routing.go), [`service_route_leases.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/service_execute.go), and [`service_session_log.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/service_session_log.go).
- Operator CLI/replay output now prints sticky bonus too in [`agentcli/routing_smart.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/agentcli/routing_smart.go) and [`internal/session/replay.go`](/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-b73fed1a-20260507T023755-5dbafdce/internal/session/replay.go).

Verification:
- `go test ./internal/routing ./internal/serviceimpl ./cmd/fiz -run "Sticky|Correlation|ServerInstance|Lease"`
- `go test ./internal/routehealth -run "Sticky|Lease"`
- `go test . -run "Sticky|Correlation|ServerInstance|Lease"`
